title: When Validators and Repairs See the Same Candidate: A Confirmatory Study of a Guarded LLM→NetOps Pipeline
abstract: We report a preregistered, paired experiment evaluating a guarded generate→validate→repair NetOps pipeline under shared_initial_candidate semantics. The run used gpt-5-mini to produce one shared initial configuration per task for N=250 synthetic intent→configuration tasks and a deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) to classify actionable misconfigurations. Under the executed adapter contract (generation_semantics=shared_initial_candidate; retrieval_augmented_generation=false; temperature=null/unset) every sampled initial candidate passed the validator (250/250 valid), no repairs were applied, and baseline and guarded final validity rates were identical (1.0). Mapping the preregistered estimand (actionable_misconfig = 1 − VALID_CONFIGURATION) yields zero actionable misconfigurations in both arms; the paired difference = 0.0 (exact McNemar two-sided p=1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI [0.0,0.0], 10,000 resamples, seed=1729). The preregistered poisoning/RAG hypotheses were not testable because retrieval was disabled in the executed adapter; we document this preregistration deviation, quantify a power/assumption mismatch (preregistered baseline ≈0.05 vs. observed actionable-misconfig rate 0.0), and discuss construct and external-validity limits (synthetic tasks, single model, single validator, no RAG). All execution artifacts, preregistration, and analysis scripts are archived with the execution manifest.

sections.introduction: Generative LLMs are increasingly proposed for NetOps tasks such as intent-to-configuration translation and staged change planning [1,2]. Because LLMs may omit ordering constraints or violate invariants, guarded architectures that pair generation with deterministic validators and bounded repairs (generate→validate→repair) are advocated as a safety control [3,4]. Prior work proposes guarded or tool-augmented pipelines and documents failure modes and adversarial risks in adjacent RAG contexts [5,6]. We preregistered a confirmatory experiment to evaluate whether poisoned retrieval contexts can induce actionable misconfigurations in a RAG-enabled pipeline. The executed run, however, used shared_initial_candidate semantics with retrieval disabled; thus the executed estimand measures the paired effect of validator+repair on the same single sampled candidate (baseline single-shot validity vs. final guarded validity after permitted repair). We report the executed design, results, and the concrete preregistration deviations that affected testability of the original poisoning hypotheses.
sections.related_work: Recent surveys and application papers document active use and proposals of LLMs for NetOps (intent-based translation, zero-touch configuration) and the rise of tool-augmented architectures that call deterministic validators or simulators [1,2,3]. Studies highlight LLM hallucination and constraint violations as reliability risks that motivate verification and repair loops [7,8]. Work in adjacent RAG/SOC domains shows that poisoned retrievals can induce targeted hallucinations, motivating NetOps-specific adversarial benchmarks [5]. Prior prototypes report empirical gains from validator augmentation in limited settings but note tradeoffs in latency and engineering complexity [4,9]. Our study contributes a tightly preregistered, paired empirical probe of a guarded pipeline under shared_initial_candidate semantics; it does not, and was not executed to, evaluate RAG-poisoning effects (see Methods).
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and executed contract: We preregistered candidate-2026-003-prereg-v1 with a paired confirmatory estimand targeting the effect of poisoned retrievals on actionable-misconfiguration rate. The frozen execution contract actually run declared: adapter_family=hosted_netops_gvr_v1, model=gpt-5-mini, generation_semantics=shared_initial_candidate, retrieval_augmented_generation=false, initial_generation_calls_per_task=1, maximum_repair_calls_per_task=1, task_count=250, planned_episodes=500. We state explicitly that the model configuration recorded temperature=null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic hosted-model sampling and does not imply temperature=0. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics exactly the same initial sampled candidate was reused for baseline and guarded arms (no independent per-condition sampling); this was enforced by the adapter and is the reason only validator/repair can create paired differences.

Tasks, validator, and scoring semantics: We used 250 deterministic synthetic intent→configuration tasks generated by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 (task manifest archived). The deterministic validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5 returns a binary validity indicator labelled in the execution bundle as scorer 'success' = VALID_CONFIGURATION (1) or invalid (0). The preregistered estimand actionable_misconfig was defined as the presence of an actionable misconfiguration; to align preregistration and archival labels we adopt the exact mapping used in the analysis: actionable_misconfig = 1 − VALID_CONFIGURATION. This inversion is an explicit preregistration-to-execution semantic reconciliation: in the stored artifacts a scorer value of 1 indicates the configuration is valid (no actionable misconfig), hence actionable misconfiguration rate equals (1 − stored_success_rate). All reported numerical results and hypothesis tests use that mapping.

Experimental procedure and analysis: For each task we obtained one shared initial generation from the model (shared across conditions). Baseline recorded validator result on the initial candidate. Guarded applied deterministic validation and permitted at most one repair attempt when the validator reported violations; final guarded result recorded the validator status after any permitted repair. Primary confirmatory test: paired comparison of actionable_misconfig indicators (paired exact McNemar two-sided; alpha=0.05). Paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples; seed=1729) produced CIs. Analysis executor paired_binary_analysis_v1 processed archived result files; all raw outputs, validator traces, and analysis code are archived in the execution bundle.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and artifacts: The run completed as recorded in the execution manifest (started 2026-08-31; completed 2026-08-31). Planned episodes 500 (2×250) completed with zero failed episodes; provider-call audit recorded 250 hosted model call events corresponding to the shared initial generation stage. Representative response and validator-trace artifacts (e.g., execution/responses/task-000004-shared-initial.txt and execution/scoring/task-000004-*.json) appear in the bundle and show identical shared initial candidates across baseline and guarded arms.

Primary confirmatory outcomes (artifact-backed numbers): Using the stored scorer semantics and the mapping actionable_misconfig = 1 − VALID_CONFIGURATION, the archived contingency counts are n11=250, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0 under the stored 'success' label (that is, VALID_CONFIGURATION=1 for all 250 pairs). Interpreting per the preregistered estimand (actionable misconfig = 1−VALID_CONFIGURATION) yields actionable-misconfig counts all zero in both arms. The paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0. Exact McNemar two-sided test p=1.0. Paired bootstrap 95% CI for the paired difference = [0.0,0.0] (10,000 resamples, seed=1729). The validator traces show repair_applied=false for every guarded episode. The analysis artifacts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/missingness_summary.csv) are archived and consistent with these numbers.

Preregistration deviation (RAG/poisoning): The preregistration targeted a poisoning-of-retrievals hypothesis and dose–response analysis across poison fractions. The executed adapter configuration had retrieval_augmented_generation=false; no retrievals (clean or poisoned) were injected. This is an explicit, recorded preregistration deviation: the poisoning hypotheses were not testable in this run and thus remain unexecuted. We document this deviation here and in the archived preregistration fidelity records.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation and limits of inference: Under the exact execution semantics (shared_initial_candidate; one sampled initial generation per task; deterministic validator; retrieval disabled) every sampled initial candidate was valid; consequently the guarded pipeline (which could only act via validator-triggered repair) had no opportunity to alter outcomes. This yields the narrow, artifact-backed conclusion: when baseline and guarded arms begin from the same single valid candidate (per deterministic validator), the guarded pipeline produced no paired change in actionable misconfiguration rate. This does not imply guarded pipelines are unnecessary generally. Instead, it clarifies that (a) a guarded pipeline's marginal benefit depends on the base rate of invalid initial candidates under the chosen model and prompt, (b) shared_initial_candidate semantics intentionally isolate validator/repair effects but prevent measurement of independent generation variability, and (c) disabling retrievals makes poisoning hypotheses untestable.

Power and assumption mismatch: The preregistered power calculation assumed a baseline actionable-misconfig rate ≈0.05 and targeted detectible paired increase delta≈0.05 (80% power at α=0.05). The observed actionable-misconfig baseline rate (after mapping) was 0.0 (no actionable misconfigs observed), violating the baseline-rate assumption and invalidating the planned sensitivity interpretation for the original poisoning hypothesis. In short: with zero observed events the preregistered power calculation does not inform the unobserved-poison effect; absence of evidence for poisoning in this run follows from retrieval being disabled and the observed zero-event outcome, not from a sensitive test of the poisoning hypothesis.

Threats to validity and generalization: Internal validity — shared_initial_candidate semantics were enforced as preregistered and archived; this isolates validator/repair effects but prevents sampling-variability measurement and therefore cannot detect differences that would arise if baseline and guarded had independent generations. Construct validity — the deterministic validator is rule-based and may omit production failure modes (vendor-specific semantics, runtime convergence). External validity — synthetic task family, single model (gpt-5-mini), single validator, and disabled retrieval limit generalization to production heterogeneity and to RAG-enabled threat models. Conclusion validity — the observed exact zero-event outcome yields precise paired bootstrap CIs here, but that precision reflects homogeneous outcomes in this controlled synthetic corpus rather than broad operational safety.
sections.conclusion: We conducted a fully preregistered paired experiment of a guarded generate→validate→repair NetOps pipeline under shared_initial_candidate semantics. The execution (gpt-5-mini; deterministic validator; retrieval disabled) produced 250/250 valid initial candidates and no repairs; consequently the guarded pipeline produced no paired change (paired difference = 0.0; McNemar p=1.0; 95% CI [0.0,0.0]). Crucially, the preregistered poisoning/RAG hypotheses were not testable because retrieval-augmented generation was disabled in the executed adapter; this preregistration deviation and a power/assumption mismatch (preregistered baseline ≈0.05 vs. observed actionable-misconfig rate 0.0) limit confirmatory inference about retrieval-poisoning. Follow-up experiments should enable controlled retrieval augmentation and poisoning injection, broaden validator realism, and evaluate independent-generation semantics to measure guarded pipelines' mitigation potential under adversarial retrievals and sampling variability.

limitations: The executed run used generation_semantics=shared_initial_candidate and one sampled initial generation per task; therefore it measures validator/repair effects on the same candidate and cannot measure independent generation variability across arms.

Retrieval-augmented generation was disabled in the executed adapter (retrieval_augmented_generation=false); the preregistered poisoning/RAG hypotheses and dose–response analyses were therefore not testable in this run and are recorded as preregistration deviations.

The stored scorer label semantics required explicit mapping to the preregistered estimand: archival scorer 'success' = VALID_CONFIGURATION (1), hence actionable_misconfig = 1 − VALID_CONFIGURATION. This semantic inversion is reconciled and applied to all reported estimands and tests.

Single LLM (gpt-5-mini) and single deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) were used; synthetic tasks and one validator limit external validity to heterogeneous production topologies, vendors, and multi-model ensembles.

The model configuration recorded temperature=null/unset; null is not evidence of deterministic sampling—model-side nondeterminism may remain and is logged in the execution artifacts. The observed zero-event outcome (no actionable misconfigs) invalidates the preregistered power assumptions (preregistered baseline ≈0.05) and therefore does not constitute a sensitive test of the originally intended poisoning effect.
